focusVocab.gloss: certain, definite; たしかに = definitely, for sure

glossary.gloss: certain, definite; たしかに = definitely

grammarNotes: V-ている — foregrounded at last. Ongoing action: 動いている = "is moving"; resultative state: 落ちている = "has fallen [and remains fallen]". The て-form from ch11/16 combined with いる.
V-dict + と — "whenever / if / when X, then Y" (automatic consequence). さわると動く = "if you touch it, it moves" (automatic every time). Distinct from the quotative と.

V-てしまう — completion, often with a shade of "oops" or "it ended up that way". 夕方になってしまった = "it's gotten late (before we knew it)"; 落ちてしまった = "went and fell". You have met this in passing since ch13 (みつけちゃった — the casual contraction ちゃう); here it is formally yours.

V-てみる — "try doing / do and see". さわってみたい = "I want to try touching it"; 見てみて = "take a look". The みる is written in kana — it is the try-auxiliary, not literal seeing. Previewed since ch14 (つかまえてみたい); now taught.
確か — can be a na-adj ("確かなこと" = "a certain thing") or an adverb ("確かに" = "certainly / for sure"). 確か, 昨日は違った = "I'm pretty sure yesterday was different."
